Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our audit team has a follow-up: we need a concise description of how Redwood enforces territory-bound (region-locked) tenants for Dedicated deployments, plus what evidence you can provide that data and snapshots can be wiped and won't replicate outside the committed region.

Specifically they're asking for:
- A short operational summary of the region-lock mechanism (how pinning works at the orchestration and storage layers)
- Evidence of one-time snapshot deletion and how long metadata/reference artifacts remain
- Drift/replication protection: what prevents cross-region replication in failover or backup scenarios
- A sample attestation we can present to internal compliance

Can you share a runbook or artifact we can attach to the audit? We're on a tight deadline (audit window opens 10/20).

Appreciate it,
Alice

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below and I attached our operational runbook snapshot for Dedicated territory-locks. If you need, Ben and Laura are copied for the deeper replication/backup details.

Quick operational summary:
- Pinning: Customers can request territory binding at deployment creation (region code). The control plane records the pin on the tenant resource; the orchestration agent enforces node placement and storage class scoping so compute and storage for that tenant are allocated only on nodes with matching region labels.
- Storage: Persistent volumes for pinned tenants are backed by region-scoped block volumes. Snapshots are stored in the same region by default; cross-region snapshot replication is disabled for pinned tenants unless explicitly enabled via a documented change request and mutual agreement.
- Deletion/Wipe: We support tenant-scoped purge which runs a three-step sequence: logical delete (metadata tombstone), snapshot deletion (remove stored snapshots and any incremental chains), then final sweep that zeroes or deprovisions underlying blocks per cloud provider APIs. Our runbook includes timing expectations and operator playbook for evidence collection.
- Failover: For Dedicated, automatic cross-region failover is off by default for pinned tenants. We offer a manual failover path which requires signed approval and will be logged, and it must pass our policy checks for data residency.

Attached artifacts: territory-lock-runbook.pdf (excerpt), replication-map.svg (topology), and a draft attestation template (redwood-attestation-20261013.pdf).

Next steps: Laura can provide the exact retention windows for snapshot metadata per provider and Ben can confirm the codepath used during tenant purge so you can include it in the audit packet. Let us know if you want a short call to walk through the runbook before 10/20.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova

Hi Alice — following up with specifics you can paste into the audit report: 

1) Snapshot metadata lifetime (typical Dedicated config):
- Immediate: when a tenant purge is initiated, snapshot objects are queued for deletion within the same region.
- 24–72 hours: background workers reconcile and remove snapshot chains; finalization depends on provider GC windows.
- 7 days: we retain logs and operation records for forensic reconstruction by default (configurable shorter on request).

2) Replication safeguards:
- Control-plane policy: replication selectors are explicit; pinned tenants are excluded from global replication groups unless a replication exception is created (requires JIRA ticket + 2 approvers).
- Storage enforcement: volumes are provisioned with region-scoped storage-class labels; our CSI driver rejects provisioning requests outside the allowed topology.

3) Evidence we can produce on request:
- Snapshot deletion trace (operation IDs, timestamps)
- Node placement report showing tenant pods/instances were scheduled only on region-scoped nodes during the life of the tenant
- Audit log bundle and signed attestation PDF

If the auditor wants carrier-grade proof, we can run a timeboxed purge on a test tenant and provide end-to-end traces and cloud provider confirmation.

Laura Bennett
Principal Product Ops | Redwood Inference

Hi Alice — quick technical clarifications to include in the attestation (and attached the signed attestation PDF):

- Cloud GC dependencies: The 24–72 hour window covers our internal reconciliation and provider GC. In practice: object snapshot deletion requests are issued immediately; many providers finalize object removal within 24 hours, but some providers may retain references or tombstones up to 72 hours before reclaiming underlying storage. We will word the attestation to reflect this dependency and avoid absolute guarantees.

- Region naming: We can produce an attestation that names the exact committed region (e.g., EU - Ireland / eu-west-1) for your Dedicated cluster. The attached redwood-attestation-20261013.pdf is pre-signed and references the committed region and the tenant identifier (we have redacted the tenant id in the demo copy; we will populate it for your tenant before final sign-off).

- Artifacts we included: territory-lock-runbook.pdf (excerpt), replication-map.svg (topology), signed attestation (attached). If you want the full runbook rather than an excerpt we can provide it under an NDA.

Let us know if you want a short review call to walk the auditor through the attachments.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Platform Security | Redwood Inference
